note.en: Rack-scale product with very limited on-demand access: CoreWeave still lists the cheapest published rate (~$10.50/GPU-hr, re-confirmed), and Azure's ND GB200 v6 bare-metal listing remains the tracked ceiling at ~$27/GPU-hr. GetDeploying's on-demand tracker has thinned to essentially that single priced hyperscaler listing, so the ~$18.79/GPU-hr blended median can no longer be independently corroborated this cycle — carried over as directional, not freshly verified. Most capacity (Together AI, Oracle, Azure) is still sold as reserved contracts with quote-only pricing; CoreWeave will quote 1-year terms on request (~35% off list) but publishes no rate card.

Floor shifted providers again: Verda's prior $3.12/GPU-hr listing no longer appears in tracked cohorts, and Packet.ai is now the best-corroborated cheapest on-demand rate at ~$3.75/GPU-hr (agreement across two independent trackers). Typical on-demand holds near ~$6.5/GPU-hr as new Blackwell capacity from Nebius, RunPod and CoreWeave keeps catching up with demand, while Google Cloud's a4-highgpu-8g stays the ceiling at $16.11/GPU-hr. No clean published 1-year rate.

Newest AMD flagship with a thin rental market: Vultr's prior $2.59/GPU-hr rate now reads as spot rather than on-demand pricing in tracked cohorts, making DigitalOcean's ~$4.50/GPU-hr the best-supported on-demand floor today. Typical price stays elevated at ~$7.15/GPU-hr, with Oracle bare metal still topping the range at $8.60/GPU-hr. CoreWeave's own pricing page no longer lists an MI355X SKU, so its $4.25/GPU-hr 1-year reservation could not be re-confirmed this cycle — carried over pending a fresh quote. Coverage is still thin (3-4 tracked providers), so treat all moves as directional.

Min from FluidStack ($2.30, re-confirmed today); typical neocloud pricing is flat at ~$4.47/GPU-hr, with two independent trackers both explicitly noting no movement over the past 90 days. Hyperscaler ceiling holds at Azure's ND96isr H200 v5, ~$13.78/GPU-hr — no reserved SKU exists for that instance. Reserved-rate listings still average ~$3.72/GPU-hr.

Widest rental market (54+ providers): marketplace/neocloud low end still ~$1.49/GPU-hr (Vast.ai), typical price flat around ~$3.30/GPU-hr as more budget-tier PCIe capacity (Thunder Compute ~$2.19) entered the pool. The hyperscaler ceiling has widened — Google Cloud now lists the top on-demand rate at $14.19/GPU-hr, above Azure's ND96isr H100 v5 reference (~$11.06/GPU-hr), which remains available but is no longer the tracked maximum. Per SemiAnalysis, 1-year contract rates were around $2.35/GPU-hr as of spring 2026; the firm's own shortage commentary points to continued month-on-month increases on the reserved side, though no fresher published number has surfaced.

Vantage — Azure ND96isr H100 v5 instance pricing

note.en: Aggressively priced for its 192GB of HBM3: TensorWave anchors the low end at ~$1.71/GPU-hr (not re-confirmed this cycle, carried over), while Azure's ND96isr MI300X v5 list price spans $6.00/GPU-hr in its cheapest regions (East US 2, West US 3) up to $12.00/GPU-hr in its priciest (Brazil South) — confirmed on cloudprice.net's regional rate table. Typical pricing stays ~$3.20/GPU-hr as mid-tier providers (Crusoe, Hot Aisle) undercut the hyperscaler premium. DigitalOcean's 12-month reserved rate holds at $1.91/GPU-hr; Cyfuture AI now shows a cheaper 12-month reserved listing at ~$1.62/GPU-hr on GetDeploying's tracker.

Legacy workhorse in steady decline: floor dropped sharply as Vast.ai's marketplace now undercuts the field at ~$0.53/GPU-hr (confirmed range $0.39-0.67 depending on host reliability), well below Thunder Compute's prior $1.09/GPU-hr anchor. GetDeploying's tracked median holds at ~$1.76-1.80/GPU-hr, with GCP a2-ultragpu still listing ~$5.07/GPU-hr at the top. Civo's tiered 80GB rate card is unaffected — $1.79 on-demand, $1.59 at 12 months, down to $1.39 at 36 months; most other contract demand has moved to H100/H200.

sources.label: Civo — NVIDIA A100 GPU cloud pricing

note.en: Min holds at Lium.io's ~$0.38/GPU-hr (Des Moines), re-confirmed today. Typical pricing looks to have moved up from the prior ~$0.90 median — three trackers now read $1.00-1.54/GPU-hr, though they disagree with each other by up to 40%, so treat this as a directional estimate pending a closer spot-check. Ceiling holds near $3.5-3.8/GPU-hr (AWS/Oracle/Replicate cluster). Civo's tiered rate card is unaffected — $1.29 on-demand down to $1.09 at 12 months and $0.89 at 36 months.

sources.label: Civo — NVIDIA L40S GPU cloud pricing

note.en: Consumer flagship on marketplaces only (no hyperscaler offering): Salad Cloud still floors the market at ~$0.25/GPU-hr, RunPod Secure Cloud unchanged at $0.99 the published top (re-confirmed directly on RunPod's own pricing page). Typical pricing sits in the ~$0.56-0.67/GPU-hr band, consistent with the prior read.

Vast.ai's marketplace floor is holding near ~$0.13-0.27/GPU-hr depending on the snapshot — marketplace pricing is volatile and hour-to-hour reads vary. Serverless-billed providers keep the ceiling near $1.61/GPU-hr (Beam, re-confirmed by AIMultiple); trackers that exclude serverless configs read a lower ~$0.74-0.77 top. Typical pricing holds flat at ~$0.41-0.45/GPU-hr — RunPod Secure Cloud's $0.69 remains well off the tracked reference points on either side.
